rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midpoint temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Shorten only the gradient to measure how the critical pairs respond to slope while bringing the last peak closer to 10 minutes. Keeping the solvent window and temperature fixed makes this a clean comparison with the scouting run.
Test a substantial temperature increase at the same gradient to shift selectivity in the poorly resolved clusters. This also creates time headroom for a shallower gradient if needed.

At 60 C, a slightly shallower gradient should improve the late critical cluster and may further separate the early pair whose order changed. The expected last peak is close to 10 minutes, limiting the time penalty.

Raise the starting organic fraction and narrow the window to permit a shallower gradient without extending the last peak beyond 10 minutes. This tests whether changing the starting conditions improves the three persistent critical pairs while retaining the early peaks.

Probe the low-temperature end to determine whether a different elution order resolves the stubborn late cluster more effectively. Using the same gradient as injections 2 and 3 isolates temperature selectivity, with the last peak expected near 10 minutes.

Test an intermediate starting fraction with a shallower slope, targeting a last peak near 10 minutes. This should strengthen late-pair resolution while showing whether the early selectivity loss at phi0 0.15 can be avoided.

Test a higher starting fraction beyond the early-pair crossover, paired with a shallower gradient to improve late-cluster resolution. The last peak should remain under 10 minutes; the main risk is compression of the early peaks.

Move beyond the early-cluster crossover at phi0 0.20 while using a shallower gradient to improve the late critical pair. This should use the remaining time headroom, but will test whether the earliest peaks become too compressed.

Explore a substantially steeper gradient to move the late cluster onto the opposite side of its observed slope-dependent crossover. The shorter run leaves time headroom, and phi1 0.70 should still elute all compounds promptly.

Test whether a modest temperature decrease improves the early cluster at phi0 0.15 without sacrificing too much late-pair resolution. Keeping injection 5's gradient isolates this selectivity effect while preserving time headroom.

Use the time headroom from injection 5 for a shallower gradient at the most favorable temperature tested. This should improve the middle and late critical pairs, with the last peak expected close to 10 minutes.

Test whether cooler conditions move the early cluster away from its crossover at phi0 0.20. The slightly steeper gradient offsets increased retention, allowing a substantially different selectivity regime to be assessed near the 10-minute target.

Refine injection 8 with a shallower gradient, using its remaining time headroom to improve the middle and late critical pairs. The early crossover may remain limiting, but the combined resolution credit could exceed the current best.
Combine an intermediate temperature with a slope between injections 5 and 12, aiming to balance both early-cluster gaps and improve the late pair. The predicted last peak is just under 10 minutes.

Fine-tune the best method to a slightly shallower slope, targeting the remaining late-pair deficit while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction.

Test whether moderate cooling at phi0 0.25 restores the compressed early pairs and moves the early cluster farther from its crossover. The slightly steeper slope than injection 9 should offset the increased retention and keep the last peak near 10 minutes.

Refine the promising high-starting-fraction method with slightly cooler conditions to improve the early cluster. A modestly steeper slope than injection 17 should offset the retention increase and keep the last peak near 10 minutes.

Raise temperature slightly from injection 17 and spend the resulting time headroom on a shallower gradient. This targets improved middle- and late-pair resolution while retaining the favorable early separation at phi0 0.25.

Fine-tune the low-starting-fraction contender with a slightly steeper slope than injection 4 to bring the last peak just under 10 minutes. This preserves its favorable early separation while removing the time penalty.

Test an intermediate temperature at phi0 0.20 to move the early cluster past its crossover. The slope is adjusted to keep the last peak near 10 minutes, testing whether early-resolution gains outweigh the expected late-pair loss.

Test whether a further reduction in slope can improve enough critical pairs to justify a modest time penalty. This checks the resolution-versus-time tradeoff around the balanced early-cluster selectivity seen at 50 C.

Refine injection 19 with a slightly steeper slope to remove its small time penalty while retaining its improved late-pair separation. This tests the narrow optimum between the promising 45 C and 50 C methods.
Test a slightly shallower slope around the best method to determine whether additional late-pair resolution outweighs a small time penalty. This directly brackets the local resolution–time optimum.

Use the final injection to test a shallower gradient at the balanced intermediate temperature. Although a modest time penalty is expected, improved resolution across several critical pairs could compensate; injection 16 remains the best measured method.
